LESSON: FORWARD ROLL AND V- BALANCE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.4: Forward Roll and V- balance
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Forward Roll and V- balance, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can forward roll and V balance be used to improve flexibility and balance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Forward Roll and V- balance together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: A learner develops originality in groups as they create safe and simple games for playing.

● Communication and collaboration: A learner develops listening and speaking skills as they speak clearly while

identifying body parts that assist in performing forward roll and V balance.

● Digital literacy: A learner develops connecting using technology as they search, download and watch video clips on

forward roll and V balance.

32

Values:
● Responsibility: A learner shows accountability as they observe safety precautions for self and others while performing

forward roll and playing simple games.

● Unity: A learner displays cooperation and team spirit while playing safe and simple games with others.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Life skill: A learner enhances tolerance as they take turns while identifying body parts that assist while performing

forward roll and V balance.

Link to other learning areas:

● Language activity: Learners apply the knowledge learnt in language activity when listening and speaking while

identifying body parts that assist in performing forward roll and V balance.

Suggested learning resources:

Plastic bottles and containers, markers, field markers, open space.
